chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Bah'r, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the boundary of prostration (sujud). He said: 'From the line of hair to the place of the eyebrow; whatever part of that area you place [your forehead on], it suffices for you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the valid area for forehead placement during Islamic prostration (sujud)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Zurarah, clarifies the jurisprudential boundary for forehead contact during sujud, establishing that the area from the hairline to the eyebrow constitutes the valid zone. This definition is crucial in Shia fiqh for ensuring the physical validity of prayer, distinguishing between the hair-bearing area and the bare forehead. It reflects the practical precision emphasized by the Imams in ritual acts, ensuring that worshippers meet the minimum requirements for prostration without unnecessary strictness.
